skill.name: ai-research-explore
skill.description: Guides bounded exploration of deep learning research candidates from a frozen current_research anchor, with source lookup, idea gating, feasibility checks, and auditable experiment artifacts.
skill.summary: Plan, rank, and audit candidate-only deep learning research experiments.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, f-strings, identifiers, and URL normalization. Real risks remain: parent-directory reference loading, outbound research lookup, subprocess orchestration, user-supplied command execution, import probes, and git worktree side effects.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle required reference material inside the skill or use marketplace-approved resource loading instead of ../../ paths.

remediation.issue: User-supplied commands are passed to execution helpers
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before baseline or variant execution and validate commands against an allowlist of safe runners.

remediation.issue: Import probes execute target repository modules
remediation.suggestion: Replace exec_module smoke checks with AST parsing or run imports only in a sandboxed subprocess with no secrets.

remediation.issue: Outbound research lookup can contact external services
remediation.suggestion: Default to cache-only lookup and require user confirmation before arXiv, DOI, GitHub, or generic URL requests.

remediation.issue: Git worktrees are created outside declared output directories
remediation.suggestion: Allow users to set an explicit workspace root and document all filesystem side effects before creating worktrees.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path construction uses git_root.parent and the code creates parent directories before invoking git worktree add. This behavior is intentional but has broad filesystem side effects.

content.value_statement: Research teams need disciplined ways to test candidate ideas without overstating results. This skill structures source lookup, idea ranking, bounded runs, and auditable outputs.
actual_capabilities: Validates a frozen current_research anchor and creates an isolated exploration workspace.
Builds source inventories from seed references, repository files, arXiv, DOI, GitHub, and web locators.
Generates and ranks bounded candidate ideas with explicit gates and score breakdowns.
Plans minimal reversible patch surfaces and source-to-target mappings for candidate work.
Runs feasibility checks, optional baseline gates, and optional short-run variant execution.
Writes campaign artifacts under analysis_outputs, sources, and explore_outputs.
limitations: It does not prove novelty, SOTA superiority, or trusted reproduction success.
It depends on a user-provided task, dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, and compute budget.
Some workflows require adjacent local skills and helper scripts to be installed.
Network lookup and execution helpers can contact external services or run local commands.

use_cases.title: Rank Candidate Research Ideas
use_cases.description: Compare several deep learning candidate ideas against a frozen benchmark and evaluation contract.

use_cases.title: Plan Bounded Experiment Runs
use_cases.description: Turn a selected idea into a reversible short-run plan with explicit artifacts and rollback notes.

use_cases.title: Audit Exploration Evidence
use_cases.description: Review source support, feasibility signals, and comparison boundaries before scaling a candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Candidate Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner campaign with one current anchor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-research-explore to review candidate-only ideas for current_research <branch or commit>. Keep the dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, and compute budget fixed.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Provided Ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these candidate ideas for <task family> on <dataset>. Rank them by expected gain, feasibility, evaluation risk, source support, and rollback ease.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Short-Run Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Execution planning after an idea is selected.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan one bounded short-run experiment for the top candidate. Preserve the frozen evaluation command and produce auditable outputs under explore_outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Govern a Full Campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced campaign with lookup, gating, and execution policy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a governed Rigor Explore campaign from this research_campaign file. Use cache-first source lookup, baseline gating, source mapping, atomic decomposition, and implementation fidelity checks.

output_examples.input: Rank three candidate ideas for a segmentation model with a fixed mIoU benchmark.
output: A ranked candidate list with hard-gate failures and score breakdowns.
A selected idea with source support, expected upside, risk, and rollback notes.
A comparison boundary explaining what evidence is still missing.

output_examples.input: Plan a short-run experiment for the selected candidate.
output: An experiment manifest with the selected idea, config overrides, planned files, and evidence references.
A smoke plan covering syntax, import resolution, config paths, and short-run command checks.
A scientific changelog that separates exploratory results from trusted reproduction claims.

output_examples.input: Audit source support for a proposed module transplant.
output: A source inventory with evidence classes for external, parsed, repo-local, and seed-only records.
A source mapping report with source repo, source file, target file, and patch class.
A recommendation to proceed, narrow the patch, or stop for a human checkpoint.

best_practices: Freeze current_research, dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, and budget before candidate work starts.
Treat every result as exploratory until source contrast, ablations, and fair comparison are complete.
Run one reversible candidate at a time and keep outputs in the declared artifact directories.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for open-ended brainstorming without a durable research anchor.
Do not present short-run gains as verified novelty, SOTA, or reproduction success.
Do not enable optional command execution or network lookup without reviewing the campaign inputs.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize for?
faq.answer: It optimizes for disciplined candidate exploration with explicit evidence, boundaries, and rollback paths.

faq.question: Can it prove a research idea is novel?
faq.answer: No. It treats novelty as a hypothesis that needs literature contrast, ablations, and fair comparison.

faq.question: Does it require a complete campaign file?
faq.answer: No. A minimal campaign needs current_research, task family, dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, SOTA reference, and budget.

faq.question: Can it run experiments?
faq.answer: Yes, but only through configured helper scripts and policies. Review commands before enabling execution.

faq.question: Does it use external network services?
faq.answer: It can resolve arXiv, DOI, GitHub, and web metadata during lookup. Cache-first and seed-only modes reduce network use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
